content.thinking:
I'm planning the full workbench scene in one pass without intermediate checks — a roughly 1.6m wide, 0.7m deep table at 0.9m height, styled with Genshin-esque cel shading, gold trim, and glowing accents, topped with alchemy items and a shelf of books, bottles, and hanging herbs. I need to check whether the builder requires a root joint or if plain parts suffice.

I'll create a single "base" joint as the root and attach everything to it, building reusable helper functions for boxes, cylinders, spheres, and lathed shapes, using cel-shaded paints for the palette. Now I'm laying out the actual geometry: tabletop, four legs, stretchers, gold edge trim, a lower shelf, and the back shelf unit uprights.

I'm designing potion bottles as lathed shapes with a glowing liquid body inside a pale glass neck, cork stopper, and gold cap ring, writing a reusable potion function to place them around the shop.

I'm also planning a book stack as simple colored boxes with gold bands and inset cream pages to suggest paper, setting up a reusable Book function for variety.

I'll write a helper function to compute rotated offsets so each part's position accounts for its Y-rotation. For the open book, I'm using slanted plane geometries with SVG text decals as page textures, offset slightly to avoid z-fighting. For the brass balance, I'm planning a lathed base disc, post cylinder, beam box, shallow dish pans with thin chain rods, and small cylindrical weights, all in gold tones.

For herbs, I'm hanging bundle cards with leaf SVGs from a rail using frames, plus a potted herb with lathed pot, soil, and standing leaf cards -- using root bone weighting since no joint is needed. For alchemical props, I'm adding a mortar and pestle (lathed stone bowl, angled rod pestle), a candle with glowing flame, a small cauldron with glowing green brew and tripod legs with bubbles, and an alembic made from a sphere and curved glass tube sweep, all bound to the root bone. Now I'm moving on to designing the crystal elements as cone shapes.

Now I'm adding cyan cryo-glow crystal clusters, rolled scrolls in cream with red ribbons, shelved jars of herbs, and gold drawer knobs on the table front. I'm also considering a cloth table runner with gold tassels and striped gold texture, and deciding whether a hanging lantern is needed beyond the candle for lighting.

I'm working out exact dimensions for the workbench (1.8 wide, 0.7 deep) and the shelf unit behind it, planning where items sit so nothing overlaps. Writing the module setup and imports...

Adding box, cylinder, sphere, and lathe geometry helpers...

Defining color palette with wood grain textures and gold cel-shaded materials...

Building the table structure...

Adding more props and drawer details...

Still positioning shelf posts and back panel...

I'm adding a gold-capped rail below the top for hanging herb bundles, positioning it to sit forward of the shelf fronts so the bundles drape in front of the top shelf items without clashing with the lower shelf's contents.

Writing leaf and lavender SVG textures...

Now I'm designing a potion-placing function with configurable shape, color, and scale, using lathe-style outline points to define round flasks, tall vials, and square bottles, plus a glass neck and glowing liquid inside.

I'm adding details like a gold collar ring, a wood cork, and a front-facing rune label plane positioned tangent to the flask's curved surface, then applying a subtle glow to the liquid part.

Now I'm sketching alternate bottle shapes—a tall vial lathe, a boxy square bottle, and a hexagonal lathed shape—to give variety as a parameterized "kind" option. I'm also working out liquid surface height relative to each container's origin, then laying out items on the bench top starting with the cauldron on the left side.

Defining the cauldron's lathe outline...

Adding tripod leg rods under the cauldron with an ember glow sphere tucked beneath, then painting the cauldron with dark iron tones and a gold rim band for detail.

Now I'm placing an open book prop on the left side, building angled page boxes atop a navy cover block to suggest pages splayed open.

I'm adding texture planes for the visible page tops, oriented to face up with the readable direction toward the back, plus small gold corner caps and a red ribbon bookmark. For the page text itself, I'm generating a simple SVG with faint tan lines to mimic writing, scaling stroke widths so they render cleanly at the output resolution.

Now I'm moving on to a balance scale prop: a lathed wooden base and post, a tilted beam with pans hanging from chains at each end, positioned near the book.

Adding chain rods connecting beam ends to pan rims, then placing brass weight cylinders in the left pan and a glowing cyan gem octahedron in the right pan.

Now I'm sketching the beam's gold end hooks, pivot sphere, and a thin pointer box extending downward from the pivot.

For the right-side vignette, I'm designing an alembic distillation setup: a glass flask with glowing purple liquid, a neck and dome head, and a sweeping tube curving toward a collecting bottle.

I'm checking the layout for spatial conflicts -- the alembic footprint overshoots the bench edge, so I'm shifting its base and collector flask inward. I also need to reposition the scale so its pans don't collide with the alembic, and then nudge the open book further left to avoid overlapping the scale's pans.

Still positioning alembic parts...

Now I'm laying out the front row of objects—cauldron, book, mortar, scale, and alembic—spacing their x and z coordinates so their bases don't overlap, adjusting radii as needed.

Still working through the back row placement...

Placing more potions and an alembic in the back right, then adding an herb pot with terracotta/teal glaze on the front right, scattering herb frame cards around it with randomized angles and positions for a natural look.

I'm adding a small mushroom cluster near the book and mortar, using hemisphere caps with white dot spheres and cream stems, plus a stone mortar bowl built from a lathe profile.

Now working out the pestle shape — a tapered rod leaning out of the mortar with a rounded ball tip.

Adding a small green paste disc inside the bowl, then sketching an inkwell-and-quill prop nearby: a tiny lathe-turned glass inkwell plus a thin angled rod for the quill shaft with a spike-shaped feather tip.

Now I'm flattening the feather using a scaled cone so it reads as a thin blade shape rather than a solid cone, oriented along the quill's tip direction. Then I'm planning a hanging lantern on the rail, with chain segments running from a mount point down to the lantern body.

Placing five herb bundles along x positions avoiding the lantern spot, each wrapped with a handful of card-frames leaning straight down at 180° with slight splay variation via different flow angles per card, keeping bend at zero and sizes small.

Now I'm designing the first shelf's contents: a row of upright standing books on the left side with varied spine thicknesses and heights, each built from a cover box plus slightly inset pages box to suggest printed page edges.

Simplifying to cover box plus spine bands and a label, with a cream strip for visible page edges on top, and maybe one book leaning slightly. I'm cycling through cel-shaded colors like red, navy, teal, purple, green and gold for the covers, with randomized heights, then moving to the apothecary jars on the right side of the shelf.

Writing jar and prop code...

Skipping the poster idea and instead giving the back panel itself a texture: a dark wood base with a gold diamond lattice pattern and faint rune circles, sized so the SVG viewBox aligns with the panel's aspect ratio for crisp strokes.

I also need floor items like a sack, basket, and barrel, plus wood grain texture on the support posts. For labels, I'm designing a small rune-style icon: a cream rounded rectangle with a gold border and a dark diamond symbol inside, sized for clarity at small scale.

Writing SVG code...

I'm estimating the part count at around 350, which should keep triangle count manageable, and considering adding a teal table runner with gold tassels across the bench, though I realize it may get hidden under other items placed on top.

I'm working through the vertical positioning so the runner and items don't visually sink into each other—settling on a bench height constant with the runner just a few millimeters thick so objects resting on it stay flush. I'm also placing the runner's width and front overhang with a draping edge and tassels dangling below.

For the drape itself, I'm positioning it in front of the drawer face with a small z-offset gap so it doesn't clip through, adding a gold trim strip near the bottom, and hanging five tassels made of a rod plus sphere from the drape's lower edge down a few centimeters. I'm deciding to keep the runner a plain solid color for now rather than adding a patterned texture.

I'll reuse a gold-diamond SVG pattern texture on the teal drape box instead, sized to roughly match its aspect ratio, while the runner top stays using a solid color. I'm bumping the glow strength slightly before moving on to coding the fire-related elements, picking a name, description, and Genshin Impact style tag, and double-checking the part options typing before committing.

Now I'm writing a potion-generating function that builds rounded bottle body shapes scaled by size, with different point arrays for each potion kind.

Still working out neck, collar, cork, and label placement geometry per bottle shape...

Now I'm figuring out how to build lying book stacks for the shelf—defining a cover box, a cream pages box slightly inset so the fore-edge peeks out, and gold spine bands.

I'm setting up a rotation helper for rotating offsets around the Y axis by angle theta, so stacked books can be angled without complicating the box placements, then planning where the floor basket sits relative to the bench and shelf posts.

Still writing basket geometry...

Still shaping crystal geometry...

Deciding against translucent glass spheres since they'd hide the sand - simpler to just use sand cones with a neck cylinder for the hourglass bulbs. Now I'm sketching a brass candle holder as a lathe shape with a stepped base and rim, plus a candle cylinder on top.

Adding a flame glow cone and wax drips, then a decorative orb on the shelf with a glowing cyan sphere held by a gold stand and torus ring. For the jars on shelf1, I'm spacing three along the x-axis and writing a jar helper that builds a cylinder body, wooden lid, gold knob, and label plane, filling them with colored contents like leaf, tan, and red.

I want a gold band under each lid too, and I'm being careful to only declare color variables I actually use to avoid unused-variable errors. Now I'm writing the book-building helper function...

Writing rotation offset logic...

Adding more book details...

Frame direction tuples should type correctly as number arrays. For hanging herbs I'm setting up rail frames with small offsets so they look naturally scattered, and planning leaf textures for lavender and maybe chili. Writing SVG code...

Then I'm checking overall bounds for the piece, adding lower-shelf props like a barrel with gold hoops and a teal ceramic jug built from a lathe profile.

Now I'm defining a helper for lying books, stacking a few on the lower shelf with cover boxes and protruding page boxes to look realistic.

Adding the gold spine band offset at the local position, then double-checking all variables like mottle, grain, ink, catmull, rng, frame, and glow are actually used before finalizing the code.
